Notes:
The guarantee letter is  is forfeited to the Greek State by decision of the Head of the relevant Regional Tourism Service, in order to meet any consumer requirements arising from their transactions with the ship brokerage office.
Before the decision to forfeit the letter of guarantee is issued, the Head of the relevant Regional Tourism Service of the Ministry of Tourism invites the company within a period of not less than one (1) month to settle the financial claims announced against it and proven by official evidence. The above deadline may be extended for an additional month by decision of the Head of the Regional Tourism Service.
If the time limit has expired without effect, the relevant forfeiture act is issued without further notice to the person concerned.
The refund to the beneficiary of the product of the forfeited letter of guarantee in favour of the Greek State is made upon submission of a final court decision. If there is more than one beneficiary and the amount of the letter of guarantee does not cover all the claims, it shall be paid to the beneficiaries in equal shares.
The decision to forfeit the letter of guarantee in whole or in part shall require the undertaking to restore it in full within a period of fifteen (15) days from the notification of the above decision.
If the aforementioned deadline expires without effect, the Certificate of of Existence of Legal Requirements is revoked by decision of the Head of the Regional Tourism Service concerned. If the undertaking repays in full the amount of the letter of guarantee within three (3) months of the decision to revoke it, the Certificate of Existence of Legal Requirements shall be cancelled. conditions shall be reissued without further procedure. Otherwise, the procedure for issuing a new Letter of Credit shall be followed.
If the letter of guarantee expires without another letter of guarantee of at least five years validity having been submitted, the Certificate of Existence of Legal Requirements is withdrawn by decision of the Head of the relevant Regional Tourism Service of the Ministry of Tourism.

5
Technical
The natural person or legal entity submitting the application must have a shop or store established for the sale of plant protection products (pesticides) that meets the requirements of Article 10 of Presidential Decree 159/2013 or warehouses supporting wholesale facilities selling plant protection products (pesticides) that meet the requirements of Article 11 of Presidential Decree 159/2013.
BOTH of the above conditions must be met in order to carry out retail and wholesale trade in plant protection products (pesticides) from the same store.
In the case of legal entities under Law 4384/2016 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 78), the above requirements must also apply to the distribution centres that the legal entity concerns maintains outside its principal place of business but within the boundaries of the region defined in its articles of association.

Labour
The applicant (legal or natural person) must employ, on a salaried basis, a scientist in charge who possesses the following qualifications and fulfils the following conditions:
Greek nationality or citizenship of one of the Member States of the European Union;
A university degree in agronomy or a degree in plant production or farm management from the Faculty of Agricultural Technology or the Department of Greenhouse Crops and Floriculture in the Faculty of Agriculture of a technological educational institute or an equivalent degree or diploma of equivalent specialisation from a Member State of the European Union or a non-EU country, on the basis of the principle of reciprocity. They may also be persons with equivalent training in another EU Member State on the sale of plant protection products (pesticides) and therefore able to ensure the same level of safety for humans, plant and animal health and environmental protection.
The person must not have been irrevocably sentenced to any penalty or have been indicted by irrevocable verdict for theft, embezzlement, fraud, extortion, forgery, crimes against morality, defamation and libel, counterfeiting, violation of Articles 5 and 12 of Law 1729/1987 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 144/1987), as amended, as well as violation of Articles 10, 14 and 46 of Law 4036/2012 or been irrevocably convicted of a crime or recurrent misdemeanour for which deprivation of their civil rights has been imposed.
The person must not hold a salaried position in the public sector or in a legal entity under public or private law, or have any other sole proprietorship requiring self-employment.
If the natural person submitting the application meets the above conditions and is also employed in the capacity of store manager, they are not required to employ another person for this purpose.
If a partner/shareholder of the legal entity meets the above requirements, the legal entity is not obliged to employ another person for this purpose.
In the case of legal entities under Law 4384/2016 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 78), the above requirement must also apply to the distribution centres that the concerned legal entity maintains outside its principal place of business but within the boundaries of the region defined in its articles of association.

Description
The procedure concerns the announcement of the practice of the profession of silversmiths, second-hand sellers, pawnbrokers and those engaged in the purchase or sale of used jewelry and fine jewelry from gold and other valuables. These professionals announce the practice at the police station of their headquarters. The relevant announcement can be submitted electronically with the personal passwords to TAXISnet and the interested party is informed about the progress of his case by e-mail.

In order to continue the exercise of the above professional or business activity, three (3) months before the end is required, a new announcement in competent police authority. The announcement is also submitted through the portal

fields.Description: The procedure concerns the announcement of the operation of a Private Vehicle Inspection Centre (I.K.T.E.O.), in the case of the transfer of the existing licence to a new owner. More specifically, it concerns the request for the issue of a new Confirmation of Lawful Operation after the transfer of the operating licence or Confirmation of Legal Operation of the Private Vehicle Inspection Centre, by the former to the new owner. In this case, a Certificate of Legal Operation of the Private Vehicle Inspection Centre is issued under the name of the new owner. Basic information Law 2963/2001 (ΦΕΚ 268/Series I), “Organisation and operation of public passenger transport by bus, vehicle technical inspection, land-transport safety and other provisions”. Articles 34 and 36 of Law 2963/2001, concerning the establishment and operation of private vehicle technical-inspection centres, are relevant, as amended and in force. Legal references https://api.et.gr/apiFEK/1/2001/268/pdf Law 3 3919 2011 32 Α Title: Principle of professional freedom and abolition of unjustified restrictions on access to and pursuit of professions. Article 3 provides for: (a) the abolition of unjustified requirements for prior administrative authorisation to pursue professions; and (b) the free pursuit of professions after three months have elapsed from notification of commencement, accompanied by the statutory supporting documents certifying compliance with the legal conditions, in accordance with the provisions applicable in each case. Legal references https://api.et.gr/apiFEK/1/2011/32/pdf Joint Ministerial Decision 26640/2298 2014 1302 Β This Decision includes, inter alia, the simplification and incorporation of the procedure for the announcement of the operation of a Private Vehicle Inspection Centre (I.K.T.E.O.), as well as the procedure for changing the Private Vehicle Inspection Centre data, in the system of the Points of Single Contact (KEP-EKE). Legal references https://api.et.gr/apiFEK/2/2014/1302

fields.Notes: For the announcement of an operation of a Private Vehicle Inspection Centre (I.K.T.E.O.), following a transfer of the existing licence or a certificate of legal service from the former to a new owner, the competent Office shall grant a certificate of legal service issued under the name of the new owner, if the request is accompanied by all the required supporting documents and if the legal requirements are met, as provided for in par. 5 of article 8 of Joint Ministerial Decision F50/48597/5875/2009  (Β΄ 1975). For the procedure of transfer, and the corresponding templates of the application, the certificate of application and the certificate of legal operation, the provisions of the circular no. 27230/2888/2012 (ADA: B4ΛX1-KΔ) and the Joint Ministerial Decision 26640/2298/2014 (B 1302) shall apply. In the event of a change in the details of the establishment and the declared personnel. the transfer request is rejected and the procedure of the announcement of the operation of the Private Vehicle Inspection Centre after the change is followed, as applicable. Description
The procedure concerns the announcement of the operation of a Private Vehicle Inspection Centre (I.K.T.E.O.), in the case of the transfer of the existing licence to a new owner. 
More specifically, it concerns the request for the issue of a new Confirmation of Lawful Operation after the transfer of the operating licence or Confirmation of Legal Operation of the Private Vehicle Inspection Centre, by the former to the new owner. In this case, a Certificate of Legal Operation of the Private Vehicle Inspection Centre is issued under the name of the new owner.

Notes
For the announcement of an operation of a Private Vehicle Inspection Centre (I.K.T.E.O.), following a transfer of the existing licence or a certificate of legal service from the former to a new owner, the competent Office shall grant a certificate of legal service issued under the name of the new owner, if the request is accompanied by all the required supporting documents and if the legal requirements are met, as provided for in par. 5 of article 8 of Joint Ministerial Decision F50/48597/5875/2009  (Β΄ 1975). For the procedure of transfer, and the corresponding templates of the application, the certificate of application and the certificate of legal operation, the provisions of the circular no. 27230/2888/2012 (ADA: B4ΛX1-KΔ) and the Joint Ministerial Decision 26640/2298/2014 (B 1302) shall apply.
In the event of a change in the details of the establishment and the declared personnel. the transfer request is rejected and the procedure of the announcement of the operation of the Private Vehicle Inspection Centre after the change is followed, as applicable.

Description
The procedure concerns the issuance of an authorisation to engage in the occupation of road haulage operator or the renewal of the authorisation to engage in the occupation of road haulage operator. In the case of an application for the renewal of the authorisation to engage in the occupation of road haulage operator due to its expiry, all the supporting documents relating to the issuance of the authorisation to engage in the occupation of road haulage operator shall be submitted, in addition to the expired authorisation (document) to engage in the occupation of road haulage operator.

Notes
The authorisation to engage in the occupation of road haulage operator shall be granted to transport undertakings established in Greece and engaged in the occupation of road haulage operator by means of motor vehicles or combinations of vehicles of any Maximum Permissible Laden Weight (MPLM) of a Vehicle. 
Transport undertakings include 
(a) natural persons residing in Greece who are nationals of a Member State of the European Union or of the Single Economic Area, or are of proven Greek descent (aliens of Greek ethnic origin) or are third country nationals who can access the occupation of road haulage operator in accordance with Greece’s international commitments, and
(b) commercial companies incorporated in accordance with Greek law and with their registered office in Greece. The authorisation to engage in the occupation of road haulage operator shall have a maximum validity of five (5) years.
Where any of the supporting documents, with the exception of the insurance policy or the certificate of insurance coverage submitted for proof of financial standing, have a period of validity of less than five (5) years, the authorisation to engage in the occupation of road haulage operator shall be issued for a period equal to the validity of that supporting document.

Conditions for non-commission of criminal offenses
The undertaking shall be of good repute. The owner of the transport undertaking must be of good repute, where the undertaking is an individual undertaking, or its legal representative must be of good repute, where the undertaking is a legal person, and, at the same time, so must the transport manager, if it is a different person. Any of these natural persons are not of good repute if
(a) they have been irrevocably sentenced to any penalty in the past 10 years prior to the submission of the application for smuggling, transport of irregular migrants, drug-related offences, sex trade, human trafficking, slave trade, sexual violence, and economic exploitation of sexual health, murder, attempted murder, fraud, theft, embezzlement, forgery, use of false documents, robbery, kidnapping, formation of a criminal organisation, terrorist act
(b) they have been irrevocably convicted at least twice in the 8 years prior to the submission of the application, with a custodial sentence of at least six (6) months for offences of a commercial nature
(c) they have been irrevocably convicted at least twice, in the 8 years prior to the submission of the application, with a custodial sentence for violations of the provisions the law on the transport of goods or passengers or professional liability
(d) they have been irrevocably convicted at least twice in the 8-year period prior to submission of the application, with a custodial sentence for violations of the provisions of the law on the salary and work conditions of the occupation;
(e) they have been irrevocably convicted at least twice during the five years prior to the submission of the application, with a custodial sentence of at least six (6) months for violations of the provisions of the Road Traffic Code;
(f) they have been irrevocably convicted at least twice in the 8 years prior to the submission of the application, with a custodial sentence of at least six (6) months, for at least two violations of the provisions of points (b), (c), and (d) above;
(g) they have been declared bankrupt during the five years prior the submission of the application. The impediment of cases (a) to (g) shall cease to exist if the penalty is commuted.

The procedure concerns the issue of an electronic responsible declaration by the person concerned, without a visit to a store of administrative authority or JEP. You can enter the e-mail address in the following two ways:
(a) by your personal web banking codes in one of the available banks
or (b) by your personal access codes at the TAXISnet (after entering once with the web banking codes, to confirm your mobile phone number)
then you will receive confirmation codes with SMSs on your mobile. The electronic responsible statement you will issue is legally equivalent to a responsible declaration bearing the authentic signature and you can either send it electronically, or print it and deposit it on a public service. At the same time, you will have the right to sign the form of the declaration of responsibility under Law 1599/86 (Article 8) and submit it to a responsible service as a reasoned submission.

In cases there is a change in the basis of the establishment, the activity provider must submit a new notification (par.5 of art.6 of Law 4442/2016)
In cases a notified activity is no longer provided, then the interested party must proceed to a change of notification in order to update the existing one.
In cases of death of the activity provider: the legal heir must change the details of the notification within 4 months of becoming aware of the induction, stating the decision number of the relevant Court of First Instance with which the will was published, as well as the certificate of the same court for non-publication of another will.
In case of a handwritten will, the above court is required to declare it as the "main one". If there is no will, the new provider must declare the inheritance registry number (articles 1956 of the Civil Code).
Until the issuance of the inheritance certificate, it is possible to declare a change of notification in the name of the interested party, provided that a declaration (or e-mail) to the relevant municipality of a certificate of close relatives and solemn declarations stating the continuation of the activity by the specific individual. The new provider is responsible for the operation of the store from the day of the declaration change.
The new Entity must present the above documents to the competent audit authorities if requested.

Description
The procedure concerns the Amendment of the Notification of the Establishment and Operation of a Food Service Establishment and is addressed to citizens and legal entities. The interested party (person or legal entity) notifies – electronically - the competent authority for (a) any changes in the Entity providing the activity or (b) any changes in the data and information already registered in the initial notification for the establishment and commencement of operations of a a Food Service Establishment at a specific place or premise.
Basic information

Notes
The interested party (person or legal entity) sends an online notification to the competent authority about the change of the activity provider or the change of the data declared during the initial notification on the establishment and opening of a Food Service Establishment (FSE) in a certain place or establishment. 
Note: 
In case of a change in the registered office of the establishment, which constitutes a change of the establishments location, the entity shall make a new notification (paragraph 5 of article 6 of Law 4442/2016).
In case of cessation of any of the activities declared in the notification, the party concerned shall also make a change to the notification.
In case of death of the entity as a person: the legal heir must change the details of the notification within 4 months from the date when he/she became aware of the induction, stating in the change of the notification the number of the decision of the relevant Court of First Instance by which the will was published, as well as the certificate of the same court on the non-publication of another will. If the will is a personal will, the above court must declare the will to be the main will. If there is no will, the new body must indicate the number of the succession (Articles 1956 et seq. of the Civil Code). Until the issue of the probate certificate, it is possible to declare a change in the notification in the name of the person concerned, provided that the certificate of next of kin and their responsible declarations on the continuation of the activity by the person concerned is declared (or sent electronically) to the relevant municipality. The new entity is responsible for the operation of the establishment from the day of the change declaration. The new operator must produce the above documents to the competent control authorities on request.

The process pertains to the Change of Notification for the Establishment and Operation of Theatres and Cinemas and it is addressed to persons and legal entities. The interested party (person or legal entity) sends an online notification to the competent authority about the change of the activity provider or about the change of its details which have been registered during the initial notification for the establishment and start-up of theaters and cinemas.

Note:
In cases there is a change of location of the establishment, the provider of the activity must submit a new notification (par.5 of art.6 of Law 4442/2016)
In cases a notified activity is no longer provided, then the interested party must also proceed to a new notification.
In cases of death of the natural person who provides the activity: the legal heir must change the details of the notification within 4 months of becoming aware of the induction, stating - during the change of the notification - the decision number of the relevant Court of First Instance with which the will was published, as well as the certificate of the same court for non-publication of another will. In case the will is special, the above court is required to declare it as the "main one". If there is no will, the new Entity must declare the bequest number (articles 1956 of the Civil Code). Until the issuance of the inheritance, it is possible to declare a change of notification in the name of the interested party, provided that a declaration (or e-mail) to the relevant municipality of a certificate of close relatives and solemn declarations stating the continuation of the activity by the specific individual. The new entity is responsible for the operation of the store from the day of the declaration change. The new Entity must present the above documents to the competent audit authorities if requested.

Description
This procedure has to do with the establishment authorisation, operating authorisation and notification of operation of recreational activities in amusement parks, circuses and ice rinks.
Basic information
Competent body

Notes
To carry out business relating to indoor or outdoor amusement park, circus and ice rink activities, it is necessary to establish and operate these facilities.
The competent licensing authority is the municipality concerned, or the Special Service for Promoting and Authorising Tourist Investments (EYPATE) of the Ministry of Tourism where such activities are to be carried out on land in a tourist port.
To establish the activity (amusement park, circus, ice rink), an establishment authorisation needs to be granted by the competent licensing authority at the request of the party concerned.
To operate the activity (amusement park, circus, ice rink), an operating authorisation needs to be granted by the competent licensing authority (municipality or EYPATE) at the request of the party concerned, or a notification needs to be submitted by the party concerned to the above licensing authority.
An operating authorisation is required to operate activities that include amusement devices falling under the scope of Decision No 50116/20.05.2020 of the Deputy Minister for Development laying down the Regulation on safety and control of amusement equipment and structures’ (Government Gazette, Series II, No 2065).
To operate activities that do not fall under the scope of the above Ministerial Decision, the party concerned should follow the procedure for submitting a notification via the electronic notifybusiness system (www.notifybusiness.gov.gr), if technically possible. Otherwise, the notification should be submitted in hardcopy or electronic format to the competent licensing authority (municipality or EYPATE) – whereas the authenticity of the signature affixed should be verified if the notification is not submitted by the activity operator personally – or at any Citizen Service Centre (KEP) operating as a Single Service Centre (EKE), in accordance with Article 7 of Law 3844/2010 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 63).
More specifically, the following shall apply:
ESTABLISHMENT AUTHORISATION:
The application for an establishment authorisation, along with the required supporting documents, should only be submitted via the Integrated Information System for Carrying Out Activities and Audits (OPS-ADE) referred to in Article 14 of Law 4442/2016 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 230), which is accessible via the Single Digital Portal for Public Administration (gov.gr – EPSP).
Up until the OPS-ADE is launched and with regard to the part relating to an establishment authorisation for amusement park, circus and ice rink activities, the notification should be submitted in hardcopy or electronic format to the competent licensing authority (municipality or EYPATE) – whereas the authenticity of the signature affixed should be verified if the notification is not submitted by the activity operator personally – or at any Citizen Service Centre (KEP) operating as a Single Service Centre (EKE), in accordance with Article 7 of Law 3844/2010 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 63).
Where the procedure is carried out at a KEP operating as an EKE, the form referred to in Annex II to Joint Ministerial Decision No 65006/27.06.2022 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 3364) should be submitted.
The licensing authority should, within 15 days from the date the application and supporting documents were properly submitted, issue the establishment authorisation or reject the request, providing the specific reasons for its rejection decision. If the licensing authority finds it appropriate, it may, before issuing the authorisation and in any case within the same 15 day deadline, carry out a site inspection to verify the actual circumstances on site, with emphasis on adjacent facilities.
If no action has been taken within the above deadline, the establishment authorisation will be presumed to have been granted, provided that operation of the activity at that particular location is not prohibited. The activity operator may request from the licensing authority a certificate to the effect that no action was taken within the above deadline.
An establishment authorisation will remain in force for 1 year from the date of issuance and may be extended once for a further 6 months, provided that the activity operator meets the following conditions:
(a) it has submitted a request, while it still has an establishment authorisation, and
(b) it has launched the procedures to implement the structures or install the equipment required for the operation of its activity.
The licensing authority should, without undue delay, communicate the authorisation and any amendments thereto to the local competent agencies, in particular the Building Agency, the Forestry Agency, the competent agencies of the Ministry of Culture and Sports, as well as any other agencies which, in the opinion of the licensing authority, need to be informed of the establishment of the activity, in order to exercise their audit duties.
Exemption from the obligation to obtain an establishment authorisation:
Activities that are temporarily carried out in a public area which has been ceded for that purpose by the competent agency or in a municipal or private area are exempted from the obligation to obtain an establishment authorisation. ‘Temporary activity’ means an activity carried out for no more than 60 days, whereas the activity may be established at the same location no more than twice a year, irrespective of the activity operator.
In such cases, the land uses determined in the town plan concerned need not be reviewed, and Joint Decision No 7034/1298/15.03.2000 of the Deputy Minister for the Interior, Public Administration and Decentralisation, the Deputy Minister for Development, and the Deputy Minister for the Environment, Physical Planning and Public Works on minimum distances for recreational activities (Government Gazette, Series II, No 368) does not apply.
No establishment is permitted in areas that are subject to special provisions on the protection of the environment and of the cultural, architectural and physical heritage.
The supporting documents for granting an establishment authorisation are listed in points 1 to 6 of the section ‘What you will need’.
OPERATING AUTHORISATION:
To obtain an operating authorisation, the activity operator should submit an application along with the required supporting documents to the licensing authority (municipality or EYPATE), providing therein its correct details, the exact location where it wishes to establish its activity and a description of its activity, also indicating the activity code number (NACE category or activity code number – KAD). The application for an operating authorisation should only be submitted via the OPS-ADE referred to in Article 14 of Law 4442/2016, which is accessible via the Single Digital Portal for Public Administration (gov.gr – EPSP). Up until the OPS-ADE is launched and with regard to the part relating to an operating authorisation for amusement park, circus and ice rink activities, the notification should be submitted in hardcopy or electronic format to the competent licensing authority (municipality or EYPATE) – whereas the authenticity of the signature affixed should be verified if the notification is not submitted by the activity operator personally – or at any Citizen Service Centre (KEP) operating as a Single Service Centre (EKE), in accordance with Article 7 of Law 3844/2010 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 63).
Where the procedure is carried out at a KEP operating as an EKE, the form referred to in Annex II to Joint Ministerial Decision No 65006/27.06.2022 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 3364) should be submitted.
The equipment must, in any event, meet the requirements of the national and Union technical legislation to which it is subject and, in the absence thereof, it must meet the requirements laid down in the General Product Safety Directive, as specified in Joint Decision No Ζ3/2810/14.12.2004 of the Minister for the Interior, Public Administration and Decentralisation, the Minister for the Economy and Finance, the Minister for Development, the Minister for Health and Social Solidarity, the Minister for Justice, and the Minister for Transport and Communications (Government Gazette, Series II, No 1885).
The licensing authority referred to in Article 2(1) should, within 30 days from the date the application and supporting documents were properly submitted, carry out a site inspection pursuant to Article 112(2) of Law 4442/2016 and issue the operating authorisation or reject the request, providing the specific reasons for its rejection decision.
Where the activities are to be carried out on land in a tourist port, the site inspection referred to in the previous sentence should be carried out on behalf of the licensing authority by the local competent Regional Tourist Service.
More specifically, where activities are to be carried out temporarily for no more than 60 days in a public area which has been ceded for that purpose by the competent agency or in a municipal or private area, the deadline referred to in the previous sentence is 10 days from the date the application and supporting documents were properly submitted.
If no action has been taken within the above deadlines, the operating authorisation shall be presumed to have been granted, provided that the activity complies with the provisions of Chapter XIX of Law 4442/2016 and the provisions hereof, and the activity operator may request from the licensing authority a certificate to the effect that no action was taken within the deadline for granting the operating authorisation.
The operating authorisation will remain in force for an indefinite period of time, except where a public area has been ceded, in which case it will remain in force for as long as the concession is in place. The activity operator must renew and keep up-to-date any supporting documents submitted during the authorisation procedure which have a limited effective period.
The licensing authority should, without undue delay, communicate the operating authorisation and any amendments thereto to competent agencies, i.e. the Building Agency, the Fire Brigade, the Environmental Agency, the Civil Aviation Authority, as well as any other agencies which, in the opinion of the licensing authority, need to be informed of the operation of the activity, in order to exercise their audit duties.
The supporting documents for granting an operating authorisation are listed in points 7 to 21 of the section ‘What you will need’.
NOTIFICATION OF OPERATION
To launch the operation of amusement park, circus and ice rink activities without any amusement devices that fall under the scope of Decision No 50116/20.05.2020 of the Deputy Minister for Development, prior notification is required in accordance with Annex I to Joint Ministerial Decision No 65006/27.06.2022 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 3364). The notification should contain the information necessary for the activity to be carried out and should be submitted by the activity operator, the latter being the sole person responsible for its contents.
Submission of notification:
The notification should only be submitted to the licensing authority (municipality or EYPATE) via the OPS-ADE referred to in Article 14 of Law 4442/2016, which is accessible via the Single Digital Portal for Public Administration (gov.gr – EPSP). Up until the OPS-ADE is launched and with regard to the part relating to the notification of amusement park, circus and ice rink recreational activities, the notification should be submitted via the electronic notifybusiness system (www.notifybusiness.gov.gr), if technically possible. Otherwise, the notification should be submitted in hardcopy or electronic format to the competent authority referred to in Article 2 – whereas the authenticity of the signature affixed should be verified if the notification is not submitted by the activity operator personally – or at any Citizen Service Centre (KEP) operating as a Single Service Centre (EKE), in accordance with Article 7 of Law 3844/2010 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 63).
Electronic submission (OPS-ADE or notifybusiness system):
Where the notification is submitted electronically via the OPS-ADE or the electronic notifybusiness system (www.notifybusiness.gov.gr), a unique number and a time stamp will be generated by the system and assigned to the notification. The file bearing a unique number will serve as proof of submission of the notification, so no registration is required.
Submission outside the OPS-ADE or the notifybusiness system: Where the notification is submitted in hardcopy or electronic format (outside the OPS-ADE or the notifybusiness system):
(a) the competent authority (municipality or EYPATE) or the KEP-EKE should, under all circumstances, receive the notification and issue a document of proof of submission, to which the submitted notification should be attached;
(b) the competent authority (municipality or EYPATE) should assign a unique serial number to the notification, which will remain the same even if the notification is modified, simply by adding an additional serial number for each change;
(c) the competent authority (municipality or EYPATE) should, without undue delay and using any means available, notify the activity operator of the serial number assigned to its notification.
No supporting documents are required when the notification is submitted. Description
The procedure concerns the issuing of a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC), a free card, which is provided to those who are actively insured by e-EFKA, in order to have access to medically necessary state care during their temporary stay in one of the 27 EU countries, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, with the same conditions and at the same cost (in some countries, free of charge) as insured persons in that country.

								1 year
Notes
The European Insurance Card does not replace travel insurance. It does not cover private healthcare, nor costs such as a ticket for the return flight to the country of origin or loss/theft of property.
In addition, it does not cover the costs if the insured person travels specifically to receive medical treatment. Finally, it does not guarantee that services are provided free of charge, as each country’s healthcare system is different; services that are provided free of charge in the country of origin may not be free of charge in another country.
N.B.: if normal residence is transferred to another country, registration is required using the S1 form instead of using the European Health Insurance Card, in order for the insured person to receive medical treatment in that country.

Title
Application for a licence for setting up and operating a heliport
Notes:
The application must be submitted in person to the mailing address of the Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority, Athens International Airport/AIA, Building 45, P.C. 190 19, Spata, or electronically (via email: info@hcaa.gov.gr) to the Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority/Directorate for the Supervision of Air Navigation and Airports/Division of Heliport Regulations and Supervision, Charts, and Obstacles. 
The application must contain: the full details of the applicant; in the case of a legal person, the application must be submitted by the legal person’s representative, together with the legal person’s articles of association.
The application must include: 
(a) the type and dimensions of the largest helicopter to be used at the heliport;
(b) a description of the site and its physical characteristics (ground-level or elevated, and whether it is located in a residential area);
(c) the meteorological conditions for conducting flights at the heliport (VMC-IMC);
(d) the intention to conduct flights at night;
(e) the intention to use visual aids and communication frequencies.
The application shall include the full name, address and contact details of the site owner, topographic maps of the area indicating the exact location of the heliport at scales of 
(a) 1:50,000, and
(b) 1:5,000, as well as the coordinates of the site in latitude and longitude (WGS 84 reference system, with an accuracy of one second of arc) and in x and y (HATT and GGRS87 reference systems), together with the elevation of the site above mean sea level (MSL).

Legitimate interest
The existence of a legal interest in initiating the procedure, through the submission of the relevant application, for setting up a heliport by a private, municipal or public entity. It shall be granted to a government agency, a natural person, or a legal person under public or private law, including local government bodies.
Pursuant to Presidential Decree 19/2009 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 35), Article 4(1, 2, 3).
Link

2
Legitimate interest
Submission of the application in person or electronically to the Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority. The application must contain: the full details of the party with a legitimate interest in setting up the heliport; in the case of a legal person, the application must be submitted by the legal person’s representative, with the legal person’s articles of association.
The application must include the type and dimensions of the largest helicopter to be used at the heliport, a description of the site and its physical characteristics (ground-level or elevated, and whether it is located in a residential area), the meteorological conditions for conducting flights at the heliport (VMC-IMC), the intention to conduct flights at night, the intention to use visual aids and communication frequencies, full name, address and contact details of the site owner, maps of the area indicating the exact location of the heliport at scales of 1:50,000 and 1:5,000, as well as the coordinates of the site in latitude and longitude (WGS 84 reference system, with an accuracy of one second of arc) and in x and y (HATT and GGRS87 reference systems), together with the elevation of the site above mean sea level (MSL). Pursuant to Article 5 of Presidential Decree No 19/2009 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 35)

Description
The procedure concerns the licensing of the establishment and operation of music institutes (conservatories, music schools, choirs, symphony orchestras and chamber music groups) which is assigned to the Municipalities, according to Law 3852/2010 "New Architecture of Local Government and Decentralized Administration - Kallikrates Program" article 94 (par. 4, case 28)
The suitability conditions/prerequisites inspection is conducted by "Building Inspection Committees for the Suitability of the Buildings of Music Schools", which consists of: 2 Technicians (Architect or Civil Engineer) and one Sanitary/Occupational Health expert.
For the Region of Attica, the Committee for the Inspection of the Suitability of Music School Facilities is established by a decision of the Minister of Culture.
For the Regions outside Attica, Committees for the Inspection of the Suitability of the Buildings of Music Schools with the same composition are appointed by Decision of the G.G. of the relevant Region.

The Music Educational Institution shall be housed in a single building or a single complex of buildings.

Urban planning
The building must have at least five 5 classrooms when it is going to shelter a Conservatory and at least three (3) classrooms when it is going to shelter a Music School or a branch. It must also have an office, a waiting area and its corridors must be at least 1m wide.
No

Technical
At least one room must have an area of 16 m2 and the rest at least 10m2.
No
No
6
Technical
The height of the rooms must be clear 2.80m and the ratio of length to width must not exceed 2:1.
No
No
7
Technical
Classrooms must have natural light and ventilation. During the night hours, abundant technical lighting is required, free from shadows (the installation is done in alignment with consultation provided by the Inspection Committee for the Suitability of Music School Building Facilities).
No
No
8
Urban planning
Classrooms are not allowed in areas that have not been designated as main use areas (basements, warehouses, lofts, garages, etc.).
No
No
9
Urban planning
The doors must open outwards and have a width greater than 0.90m. In cases of old buildings (eg under reservation) the most appropriate solution will be indicated by the competent building control committee.
No

10
Urban planning
The music school must have at least two toilets (separate for boys and girls) that meet the hygiene/sanitary requirements. The sanitary equipment must be white and the walls must be covered with white tiles, up to a height of 1.80m. They must have natural or artificial ventilation, as well as safety lamps.
No

The use of flammable materials for decoration (curtains, carpets, nylon, etc.) is not allowed.
No

For natural persons or the members of the Board of Directors Commission or Association of Legal Persons: they must not have been convicted of insanity or any criminal offense.

For the establishment of a REIC through GEMI, a special-purpose operating licence is required, granted by decision of the Board of Directors of the Hellenic Capital Market Commission. This is not a standard citizen request, and an organised and detailed file is submitted with the application, covering the organisation, procedures and personnel of the company under incorporation.
The following shall be assessed: The suitability of prospective shareholders (legal and natural persons) as regards their honesty/integrity and financial standing. It is very likely that there will also be foreign shareholders from within and outside the European Union.
The scope of the assessment varies depending on the percentage holding of each prospective shareholder. Each prospective shareholder with a qualifying holding is assessed individually.
The suitability of the individuals who will manage the company in terms of honesty and integrity, and the necessary knowledge and experience. The structure and organisation of the applicant company in relation to the requirements laid down by specific laws, European regulations, and ministerial and HCMC decisions.
As an indication of the supporting documents required, reference is made to the annex to HCMC Decisions 3/452/1.11.2007 and 4/452/1.11.2007, which can be consulted by browsing the attached HCMC link containing the 2007 decisions.

Notes
By decision of the Municipal Council, the municipal public spaces authorised to use and the levying of the respective fees have been predetermined as follows:
A) Imposition of an annual fee per square metre, regardless of the time of use and depending on the area of the city in which the used space is located. The mayor shall issue the annual use permit, which shall specify the location and area of the space to be used, the type and duration of the use and the corresponding fee. The granted licence may be renewed by the mayor at the request of the person concerned.
B) Imposition of a monthly fee, per zone and per square metre, in cases of occupation of a pavement or road by those carrying out any kind of technical and construction works. The mayor shall issue a permit for this use.
C)Imposition of a fee for the temporary use of public spaces for up to ten (10) days for the conduct of social solidarity events or actions of tourism, cultural, artistic or public commercial promotion, which depends on the public benefit or not of the event. The mayor shall grant the relevant licence for use by the mayor.
-For the collection of the fee a note is drawn up by the beneficiary municipality and the fee is paid to the municipal treasury before the delivery of the license, as follows: 
Ιn cash, by writing the number of the collection slip on the licence.
By means of a letter of guarantee in the same amount, with the number of the letter of guarantee and the instalments by which it is to be paid being indicated on the licence. In the event of late payment of the instalments, the letter of guarantee shall be forfeited.
In equal installments within the year, provided that the obligor pays a percentage of the annual fee of not less than thirty percent (30%) and the number of installments to pay the remaining amount.

The same procedure shall be used to grant authorisations for the establishment of private LNG and/or L-CNG service stations. The installation of private LNG and/or L-CNG service stations must comply with the terms and conditions relating to safety issues, and the relevant authorisations shall be granted following the submission of the required documentation in accordance with the relevant provisions (Joint Ministerial Decision 188543 (Government Gazette 3368 B 2022), Articles 9 (paragraph 8), 12, 13 and 14).
A pure LNG and/or L-CNG service station or a mixed LNG and/or L-CNG and liquid fuels and/or CNG service station for private use is defined as an LNG service station, which the natural or legal person having the right to operate it uses to refuel a specific use and number of wheeled vehicles, as defined in the relevant provisions (Article 9 of Joint Ministerial Decision 188543 (Government Gazette 3368 B 2022)).

Application for an operating licence: For the granting of an operating licence for a pure or mixed LNG and/or L-CNG service station, the natural or legal person shall submit an application to the relevant regional Transport and Communications Authority (licensing authority) before the expiry of the establishment or extension of the licence.
The application by the natural or legal person shall be submitted together with the supporting documents required in accordance with the relevant provisions. In the case of a legal person, the application shall be submitted by the legal representative as appropriate.
For the operating licence: The application can be submitted electronically (by email), accompanied by the required documents.

Description
The procedure concerns notification about operating parking areas for heavy-duty vehicles (Article 200 of Law 4442/2016), the supporting documents kept at the premises where the activity is carried out, the method of communicating the particulars in the event of an imminent change, the authorities to which the notification is given and the changes thereto, as well as the stamp duty and penalties for the notification of these establishments. It also concerns notifications about a change of operator.
Heavy-duty vehicles are vehicles in categories M2, M3, N, N1, N2, N3, O, O1, O2, O3 and O4 (Article 198 of Law 4442/2016). These include different types of buses, trucks, trailers, semi-trailers, tankers, articulated and train-type vehicles, motor vehicles and trailer caravans.

Notes
A notification is required: (a) before starting to operate a parking area for heavy-duty vehicles and (b) before changing any part of the initial notification about operating a parking area.
Heavy-duty vehicles are vehicles in categories M2, M3, N, N1, N2, N3, O, O2, O3, O4 and O1 Annex II to Joint Ministerial Decision No 29949/1841/28.9.2009 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 2112). Parking areas for heavy-duty vehicles do not include intercity bus stations and loading and unloading bays for trucks referred to in Article 9 of Presidential Decree 79/2004 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 62), pursuant to Article 198 of Law 4442/2016.
Authorisation of any additional establishment, such as those referred to in Article 11 of Ministerial Decision No our ref.  44662/454/2019 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 2192), will be carried out separately and independently of the notification about a parking area for heavy-duty vehicles and in accordance with the legislation in force at the time Article 3(8) of Joint Ministerial Decision No 314290 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5269, 12.11.2021).
If there is an infringement relating to a notification about such operations and non-compliance with the operating requirements, the provisions on penalties laid down in Article 203 of Law 4442/2016 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 230), as specified in Article 8 of JMD No 314290 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5269, 12.11.2021), will apply.
After submitting the notification, the operator is obliged to register and issue a Certificate of Registration for the parking area in the Digital Register of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transportation, in accordance with Ministerial Decision No our ref. 329369/2023 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 6458), which replaced the previous Decision No our ref.  59388/940/2020 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5407).
The Certificate will be re-issued following any notification of change Article 6(2), of Ministerial Decision No our ref. 329369/2023 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 6458).

Title
Notification about operating Article 200 of Law 4442/2016 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 230)) parking areas for heavy-duty vehicles
Notes:
Notification about starting to operate a parking area for heavy-duty vehicles will be made in accordance with the form (application) included in the Annex to Ministerial Decision No 314290 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5269/12.11.2021). The same form is also used for notifications of any change to the initial operation of the parking area, such as a change of particulars, operator, place of activity, etc.
Especially in the case of a change of operator pursuant to Article 9 of Law 4442/ 2016 (Government Gazette, Series I, No 230), both the old and the new operator will each submit a notification about the change within ten (10) days of the change.
The notification must contain the necessary information on the activity being carried out and must be submitted by the operator, who will be solely responsible for the information contained therein (Article 3 of Ministerial Decision No 314290/2021, Government Gazette, Series II, No 5269). No supporting documents are required when submitting the notification.
The parking area operator must keep the required supporting documents referred to in Article 4 of Decision No 314290/2021 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5269), together with proof of submission of all notifications of operation of the facility, at the place where the activity is carried out, as well as the certificate of registration of the parking area in the Digital Register of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transportation.

Description
The procedure concerns the announcement of commencement and the granting of a certificate of compliance with the legal conditions for the operation of:
(a) vine stock nurseries and
(b) undertakings producing and marketing propagating material of agricultural plant species:
- seed production undertakings;
- type A, B and C nurseries; and
- type A and B undertakings marketing propagating material.
It also concerns the procedure for reviewing compliance with the legal conditions for the operation of the above undertakings and changes in the status of the above undertakings and the removal of the above undertakings from the register.

The irrigated land shall be free from any developed trees or shrubs, it shall be in favourable climate conditions and not have been used for vine cultivation purposes at least in the last ten (10) years.
In terms of plant health, it shall not be in a zone that is affected by communicable diseases or pests, especially nematodes. Soil samples shall be taken by the scientist and sent to a laboratory for nematode testing (for vine stock nurseries).

Type A, B and C nurseries shall be installed on irrigated land, whether privately owned or not, free from any developed trees or shrubs, and the land should be in favourable climate conditions.
In terms of plant health, the soil must not be in a zone that is affected by communicable diseases or pests, and must be free from nematodes. Soil samples must be taken by the scientist and sent to a laboratory for nematode testing. In cases where disinfected crop substrates (mixed soil) are used, as defined in Article 1(2)(e) of Law 1565/1985 (GG I/164), sampling and analysis of the substrate is not required (for undertakings producing and marketing or marketing propagating material).

Conditions depending on the undertaking category:
a) Seed production undertaking: It has the appropriate infrastructure, namely the facilities for the processing, packaging and storage of propagating material, with machinery appropriate to the specialisation of the undertaking, such as greenhouses or cages for vegetable seed production, where necessary.
b) Type A, B, C nurseries: It has facilities and machinery that correspond to the groups of propagating material and the plant species whose propagating material is produced.
c) Type A marketing of propagating material: It has storage and packaging facilities and mechanical equipment corresponding to its activities.
d) Type B marketing of propagating material: It has storage facilities appropriate and corresponding to its activities (for undertakings producing and marketing or marketing propagating material).

Conditions depending on the undertaking category:
a) Seed production undertaking: It has a seed analysis laboratory with germination control rooms, precision hygrometers, as well as auxiliary technical equipment. Where the undertaking is engaged exclusively in the reproduction of potato tubers for planting, the conditions laid down in the preceding passage do not have to be fulfilled.
It has a safety storage chamber for basic propagating material and previous generations, provided that material of the categories referred to in Article 3(2)(b) and (c) of Law 1564/1985 is reproduced.
b) Type C nursery: It has a tissue culture laboratory with a satisfactory degree of isolation from the other areas of the undertaking. It must include the following areas:
1. a preparation area,
2. utility areas,
3. a refrigeration room or refrigerator,
4. crop growing room and 5. aseptic tissue and crop cutting area.
Its equipment must include:
1. an aseptic bank or aseptic area;
2. a sterilisation device for nutrients, crop tools and containers;
3. PH metre;
4. stereoscope;
5. scale; and
6. Water distillation or deionisation device.
c) Type A marketing of propagating material: It has a laboratory to determine the germination and specific purity of seeds.
This obligation does not apply to any undertaking marketing propagating material which markets exclusively propagating material of agricultural plant species, other than seeds, which does not require checking its germination and specific purity. Technical
All building requirements and obligations of the current institutional framework for the establishment must be met: - The total area of the gym / sports school:
(a) is equal to or greater than 100sqm, not including outdoor and semi-outdoor areas and ancillary areas (storage, lift, boiler room, etc.); and
(b) has the necessary structural adequacy. - The total usable area used by the trainees for training or learning a sport shall be equal to or greater than 70 m2 . - The minimum height of each space shall be 2,6 m. - The minimum usable area per trainee shall be 5 m2 . - The building shall have at least 2 changing rooms with provision for the safety of personal belongings and a minimum area of 50 m2 per trainee. - Exercise or training of the trainees shall not take place in underground areas which are classified as ancillary by the provisions of the General Building Regulation. - The operation of the fitness centre does not produce sound emissions and does not cause nuisance to residents. - There is a bathroom with at least 2 hot and cold water fountains for each changing room. - There is a plumbing system for cleaning and draining the toilets and sanitary toilets. Natural or artificial ventilation Covering with durable tiles over the entire surface of the walls at least up to a height of 1,70 m. - Durable and non-slip coating over the entire surface of the floors, Doors opening from the outside inwards. At least one washbasin per two toilets. - Operation of 2 toilets (one mens and one womens) for exercisers for a capacity of up to 80 exercisers and operation of an additional toilet for each additional 40 exercisers.

With regard to the owner or legal representative (for cases of legal entities of private law): The applicant must not have the status of civil servant at a local authority or of an official legal entity of public law; he/she must not have been convicted or tried by final judgment for a felony, theft, embezzlement, fraud, extortion, forgery,  disloyalty of a lawyer, bribery, oppression, disloyalty in connection with official duties, misconduct,  crime against sexual freedom or economic exploitation of sexual life, trafficking, possession and use of drugs, even if the offence is time-barred he/she must not have been deprived of his or her civil rights as a result of a conviction not be subject to deprivation of legal aid (full or partial) or subsidiary legal aid (full or partial) or a combination of the two, on account of mental or psychological disorder He/she must not have been convicted of the criminal and disciplinary offences of pharmacostimulation pursuant to Articles 128 G and 128 I and 130 of Law 2725/1999, as the three articles were added respectively by Articles 58, 59 and 60 of Law 2725/1999. 3057/2002 (Α΄239).
He must be up to date with regard to tax and social security, and the legal entity of private law. must be up to date with regard to tax and social security.

Those eligible to operate a driving school or branch thereof are:
a) natural persons with a valid certificate for lawful practice of the profession of driving instructor.
b) legal persons, where one (1) of their members or at least one (1) of their staff has the status of instructor of candidate drivers and also holds a valid certificate for lawful practice of the profession of driving instructor.

Building
The KETHEYO shall consist of at least three (3) separate areas, including one (1) reception area, one (1) classroom and one (1) WC. The premises of the KETHEYO must have the KETHEYO as primary use, must be a single space and not part of a residence. The reception area must be well lit and have adequate ventilation.
The classroom must meet the ratio of 2.0 m²/person, which also determines the maximum number of trainees, rounded down to the nearest whole number.
The classroom must also be a single space, have good lighting, adequate ventilation, good heating and adequate soundproofing.
The WC must be directly accessible from the reception area.
KETHEYOs may not operate in a building that houses the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport or the Directorates of Transport and Communications and Vehicle Technical Inspection Centres (KTEO) of the country’s regional units.

Professional
The management of studies and responsibility for the proper functioning of the KETHEYO and compliance with the relevant legal provisions is entrusted to a Director of Studies, who must be a car and motorcycle driving instructor with a valid certificate for practising the profession.
No
No
7
Educational
Car and motorcycle driving instructors with a valid certificate for practising the profession may teach at KETHEYOs. Instructors who have had their certificate for practising the profession of instructor revoked due to physical incapacity may teach.
Also eligible to teach are holders of university or technical educational institute degrees or diplomas from Greece or abroad – recognised as equivalent schools – with specialisation in the subject matter to be taught, as follows:
a) For topics relating to vehicle mechanical or technical issues, driving technique, active and passive safety systems and methods, and environmental protection/energy saving, the prospective instructor must hold a degree or diploma from a university or higher technical educational institute or equivalent school whose graduates have the right to undertake engineering projects, or in another field related to the above topics.
b) For topics related to medical conditions and driving, road accident first aid, instructors must hold a degree or diploma from a university or higher technical educational institute or equivalent school, in medicine or nursing.
c) For topics related to road traffic legislation and social conduct/education of drivers, instructors must hold a degree or diploma from a university or higher technical educational institute or equivalent school of Law, Social Sciences or another field relevant to the above topics. Additionally Greek police officers with proven experience in traffic directorates or departments may provide instruction on the above topics.
d) The topics referred to in cases a, b, and c may also be taught by holders of a degree or diploma from a university or higher technical educational institute or equivalent school in a field other than the ones mentioned above, if they have completed training at a vocational training institute in the ‘Driving Instructor’ department.
A list of the names and qualifications of the centre’s director of studies and teaching staff shall be posted in a prominent position within the KETHEYO premises.

In the case of shared premises, the following are also required:
a) Compliance with all of the requirements for operating the above schools/centres, in accordance with the applicable legal provisions.
b) Use of different classrooms if class times overlap.
c) The reception area and common spaces of the above schools/centres may be shared, but must be separate from classrooms. Use of auxillary spaces must not disturb the use of classrooms.

Road assistance requirements: The road assistance undertaking has at least one (1) private vehicle (platform, crane) per continental regional unit of activity as well as in the islands operating, weighing more than four (4) tons, which has an installed geo-location system (GPS). Except for the above minimum mandatory vehicles, the road assistance undertaking may have an unlimited number of vehicles (such as cars, lorries or bicycles).
Road assistance vehicles are wholly owned by the road assistance undertaking or are held with the retention of ownership or rental or leasing contract. If the undertaking is only a road assistance undertaking of heavy good vehicles, then, instead of the above vehicle, it must have at least one truck of above ten (19) tons (platform, crane).

Conditions for staging and transhipment areas: The company must have at least one stay and transhipment station in each Regional Unit of mainland Greece, as well as in the islands that operates. The accommodation and transhipment station must have: a) ground floor space for office and waiting room, capable of taking passengers; b) at least one WC; c) at least one telephone connection; d) wireless communication device with road assistance vehicles; f) housed ground floor area of a competent area, with inspection or lifting machine, g) parking area for the vehicle of the undertaking.

The non-insurance company of road assistance shall have individual or group occupational liability insurance against its customers for physical damage and material damage to the provision of road assistance services. Professional liability insurance covers the business, its premises and the staff and equipment it uses. The minimum amount of cover per accident is set equal to the amount of cover for liability in the event of an automobile accident pursuant to Article 6 of PD 237/1986 (A 110).

The natural person who is the operator of the activity or the natural persons representing the legal person must not have been irrevocably convicted of smuggling, trafficking or use of drugs, human trafficking, intentional homicide, attempted homicide, fraud, theft, forgery, use of forged documents, robbery, desertion, embezzlement, usury, bribery.

Conditions for technical staff: The roadside assistance company shall employ at least the following technical staff on a full-time or part-time basis, in any form of employment relationship and under full-time or part-time contracts:
(a) A director of the technical department, a mechanical engineer, a graduate of a higher or higher school, who provides his services mainly at the headquarters of the company.
(b) In each continental Regional Unit, in the Regional Units of Crete and in the islands of Euboea, Rhodes, Lesvos, Zakynthos, Kefalonia, Chios, Kos where it operates there must be at least four employees of whom at least 50% are specialised engineers or electrician drivers and the rest drivers.
(c) Companies offering roadside assistance on islands other than those mentioned above must have at least two employees of which at least 50% must be qualified as mechanics or electricians and the rest as drivers.
(d) One mechanic or electrician driver in the at its disposal.
The minimum technical staff may include and count the owner or owners of the business, provided they have the qualifications of article 2 of Law no. 3651/2006. For the calculation of the minimum number of staff, the Regional Units of the Central, North and South Sector, Western Sector and Southern Sector of the Region of Attica (former Prefecture of Athens) shall be counted as one Regional Unit.

In cases of co-location, the following requirements must also be met:
a) all the operating conditions of the above Schools/Centres, as provided for in the relevant provisions, must be complied with
b) different classrooms must be used if their curricula coincide in terms of scheduling
c) the reception area and the common areas of the above Schools/Centres may constitute a single space, but must in all cases be different from the classrooms. The use of ancillary spaces must not interfere with use of the classrooms.
Undertakings carrying out administrative operations under KAD 9609.19.11 and insurance intermediary and insurance broker operations under KAD 66.22.10.01 and KAD 66.22.10.05 may also be co located, insofar as they belong to the same natural or legal person.

The notification procedure has replaced the Special Operation Mark. The planned inspection of the lawful operation of the accommodation facilities shall be carried out on an ex post basis by the competent authorities.

Notes
The procedure is carried out by the competent Tourism Service (Regional Tourism Services or Special Service for the Promotion and Authorisation of Tourism Investments (EYPPATE)) of the General Secretariat for Tourism Policy and Development.
1. The fees are calculated according to the capacity (number of rooms) of the tourist accommodation establishment. The maximum cost cannot be determined in advance because it depends on the number of rooms in the tourist accommodation establishment.
2. The main tourist accommodation facilities must have an approved distinctive title.
3. Hotels and organised tourist camping sites must, within 50 days of their notification of operation, issue a classification certificate from the Hellenic Chamber of Hotels.
4. NB! The notification of the swimming pools of the tourist accommodation is now submitted with the notification of the tourist accommodation establishment in the MIS 
https://openbusiness.mindev.gov.gr/
, provided that the operator of the tourist accommodation establishment is the same as the operator of the swimming pool. The documents relating to the swimming pool are specified in procedure MITOS 357446.

Notes
Prior notification is required to start a vehicle roadside assistance partner. The notification shall be submitted to the Directorate of Transport and Communications of the Regional Unit of the headquarters of the roadside assistance partner.
The notification shall contain the necessary information on the activity carried out and shall be submitted by the operator of the activity, who shall be solely responsible for the information contained therein. The notification shall not be accompanied by any supporting documents.
The roadside assistance partner shall keep the supporting documents and proof of submission of the notification at the place of activity. After submission of the notification.

Title
Notification of the operation of a vehicle roadside assistance operation
Notes:
Interested parties shall submit the initial notification/notification of change/notification of termination via the online system openbusiness.mindev.gov.gr. Until this possibility is implemented, the notification shall be submitted in paper or electronic form to the Directorate of Transport and Communications of the Regional Unit of the headquarters of the roadside assistance partner or to any KEP that operates as a Point of Single Contact (EKE). If the details of the original notification of the roadside assistance partners operation are to be changed, the partner shall submit a prior notification of the change using the same procedure as the original notification.

Conditions for roadside assistance of vehicles: The roadside assistance partner shall have at least one (1) privately owned truck (platform, tow truck) per continental Regional Unit of operation and on the islands where it operates, with a gross weight of more than four (4) tons, which has a geospatial positioning system (GPS) installed. In addition to the above minimum mandatory vehicles, the roadside assistance partner may have an unlimited number of vehicles of any kind (such as cars, trucks or two-wheelers).
The roadside assistance vehicles shall be wholly owned by the roadside assistance partner or held under retention of title or under a lease or leasing contract. If the partner is only a heavy vehicle roadside assistance partner then, instead of the above vehicle, it must own at least one (1) truck over nineteen (19) tons (platform, tow truck).
No

Building
Conditions for staging and transhipment areas: The roadside assistance partner has at least one (1) waiting and transhipment station in each P.E. of mainland Greece and on the islands where it operates. The waiting and transhipment station must have:
(a) a ground floor office and waiting room, with sufficient space for the reception of the passengers of the vehicles
(b) at least one WC
(c) at least one telephone connection
(d) a computer
(e) a device for wireless communication with roadside assistance vehicles
(f) a covered ground floor area of sufficient size, with a trench inspection pit or lifting equipment g) parking space for the roadside assistance partners vehicles.
The space must be legally existing with respect to the construction and use as a vehicle roadside assistance partner and must meet all requirements to operate as a vehicle roadside assistance partner in accordance with the applicable building and building code regulations, the fire protection regulations, the general and specific planning regulations in force at the time, as well as the building specifications of the legislation specific to the activity. The supporting document Certificate of the main use of the premises by a private engineer is not required for roadside assistance undertakings for vehicles already operating with a certificate of legal operation or a licence and submitting a notification of change pursuant to Article 213 par. 1 ν. 4442/2016 (A108). For the calculation of the minimum number of waiting and transfer stations the P.E. Central Sector, North Sector, West Sector and South Sector of the Region of Attica (former Athens Prefecture) are counted as one Regional Unit.

Conditions for non-commission of criminal offenses
The natural person who is the operator of the activity or the natural persons representing the legal person must not have been irrevocably convicted of smuggling, trafficking or use of drugs, trafficking in human beings, intentional homicide, attempted homicide, fraud, theft, forgery, counterfeiting, use of forged documents, robbery, desertion, embezzlement, usury, bribery.

Conditions for technical staff: The roadside assistance partner shall employ at least the following technical staff on any type of employment relationship and on full-time or part-time contracts:
a) In each continental P.E., in the P.E. of Crete, but also in the islands of Evia, Rhodes, Corfu, Corfu, Lesvos, Zakynthos, Kefalonia, Chios, Kos, where they operate, at least four (4) employees, of which at least 50% must be qualified as mechanics or electricians and the rest as drivers.
b) Partners offering roadside assistance on islands other than those mentioned above, at least two (2) employees, of which at least 50% must be qualified as mechanics or electricians and the rest as drivers. (c) One (1) mechanic or electrician driver in the (1) one (1) electrician and electricians technician (electricians and engineers) at the waiting and transhipment stations at their disposal.
The minimum technical staff may include and count the owner or owners of the roadside assistance partners business, provided they are qualified in accordance with Article 2 of Law No. 3651/2006.
For the purpose of calculating the minimum number of staff, the Regional Unit of the Central Sector, Northern Sector, Western Sector and Southern Sector of the Region of Attica (formerly the Prefecture of Athens) are counted as one Regional Unit.

To comply to all the building conditions and obligations according to the current institutional framework:
- The total area of the gym / sports school:
a) is an area equal to or greater than 100sq.m, not including outdoor and semi-outdoor areas and auxiliary areas (storage, elevator, boiler room, etc.) and
b) has the necessary static adequacy.
- The total useful space used by the trainees for training or learning a sport is of an area equal to or greater than 70sq.m.
- The minimum height of each space is 2.6m.
- Minimum area of useful space per trainee is 5sq.m.
- The building has at least 2 locker rooms with provision for the security of personal belongings and with a minimum area of 50 sq.m. per trainee
- The  exercise of the trainees is not carried out in underground spaces which are characterized as auxiliary by the provisions of General Building Regulations (G.B.B.)
- The operation of the gym does not produce sound emissions and does not cause nuisance to the locals.
- There is a bathroom with at least 2 sprinklers for hot and cold water for each locker room
- Existence of hydraulic installation for cleaning and drainage of toilets as well as sanitary basins. Natural or artificial ventilation lining with durable tiles on the entire surface of the walls at least up to a height of 1.70 m.
- Durable and non-slip coating on the entire surface of the floors, Doors that open from the outside to the inside. At least one sink per two toilets
- Operation of 2 toilets (one for men and one for women) for the trainees for a capacity of up to 80 trainees and operation of an additional lavatory for every additional 40 trainees

Description
The procedure concerns the notification of the commencement  of  operation of intercity bus stations (article 189 of Law 4442/2016), without fuel pump installations, the supporting documents kept at the place of activity, the procedure of notification of  data in case of an imminent change, the authorities to which the notification shall be communicated and any relevant changes. It also concerns the notification of a change of activity. 
The stations are divided into categories according to the annual number of passengers
embarking or disembarking each year:
category 1 (up to 150.000 passengers),
category 2 (from 150.000 to 1.000.000 passengers),
category 3 (from 1.000.000 to 3.000.000 passengers),
category 4 (from 3.000.000 to 10.000.000 passengers),
category 5 (from 10.000.000 and above).

Title
Notification of the commencement of operation entitled: NOTIFICATION  OF OPERATION OF INTERCITY BUS STATIONS (article 191 of Law 4442/2016 (A 230)
Relevant link

Notes:
The notification of the commencement of operation of an intercity bus station is made in accordance with the template of the annex of the Ministerial Decision No 313214 (GG B 5271/12.11.2021).
The same template also applies to the notification of any change in the initial notification for the operation of the station, such as change of data, change of operator, change of place of activity, etc.
The notification includes the necessary information on the activity carried out and is submitted by the operator of the activity, who is solely responsible for the information contained therein.
No supporting documents shall be submitted with the notification.
The operator of the intercity bus station must keep the required supporting documents, as referred to in article 4, of Ministerial Decision No 313214/2021 (GG B 5271), together with proof of submission of all notifications of the start of operation of the establishment, at the place where the activity is carried out.

Description
The procedure concerns the actions to be taken by the operator of the tourist accommodation if the accommodation includes swimming pools. The necessary supporting documents must be registered and posted to the OPS platform; during operation, the operator must maintain a file with all the required documentation for the operation of the swimming pool, which it must present when requested by the competent inspection authorities.
If the same entity operates the tourist accommodation and the swimming pool, the notification regarding the swimming pool installed at the tourist accommodation shall be submitted during the tourist accommodation notification phase. In the case of a subsequent addition of a new swimming pool, the notification of the tourist accommodation must be amended, and a new fee must be paid.
