Μeasures for active fire protection must be in taken, according to the relevant risk category.
Category A – Low Risk
This includes:
i) public gathering places with a theoretical population (as calculated on the basis of the applicable fire-fighting legislation) less than or equal to 150 persons that do not use LPG (bottles or tanks) for their operational needs;
ii) shops (food retail or service shops) with an area of less than or equal to 1,000 square meters.
iii) Funeral homes
Operators of activities belonging to category A and housed in existing buildings (building permit before 02/1989), are exempted from the obligation to prepare an active fire protection study - floor plans and a summary study of LPG storage. Exceptions are made in cases where it is impossible to comply with the terms of the provisions and deviations are requested.
In new buildings (building permit after 02/1989) the obligation to prepare and submit a passive and/or active fire protection study where required is still in force, in accordance with the provisions of article 15 of the PD 71/1988 (GG 32A) as in force.
Category A operators are exempted from the obligation to obtain an (active) fire protection certificate, but must comply with and maintain the fire protection measures and means required by current legislation, which will be reflected in floor plans that are part of the file to be kept in the holding.
Category B - Medium Risk
This includes:
i) public gathering places with a theoretical population (as calculated on the basis of the applicable fire-fighting legislation) of more than 150 persons as well as public gathering places regardless of capacity that use LPG (bottles or tanks) for their operational needs and
ii) stores (food retailers or service stores) of over 1.000 square meters as well as stores, independently of their area, that store LPG cylinders over 200 kg.
In category B, the operators must, within fifty (50) days from the date of submission of the notification, take all the necessary actions in order to be provided by the relevant Fire Service with an (active) fire protection certificate, which will be kept in the business file.
Category C - High Risk
This includes: Theatres and cinemas. 
In category C, the operators must, before the date of submission of the notification, take all the necessary actions in order to have been provided by the relevant Fire Service with a certificate of (active) fire protection which will be kept in the installation file.

Health
Μeasures for active fire protection must be in taken, according to the relevant risk category
Category A – Low Risk
This includes:
i) public gathering places with a theoretical population (as calculated on the basis of the applicable fire-fighting legislation) less than or equal to 150 persons that do not use LPG (bottles or tanks) for their operational needs;
ii) shops (food retail or service shops) with an area of less than or equal to 1,000 square meters.
iii) Funeral homes
Operators of activities belonging to category A and housed in existing buildings (building permit before 02/1989), are exempted from the obligation to prepare an active fire protection study - floor plans and a summary study of LPG storage. Exceptions are made in cases where it is impossible to comply with the terms of the provisions and deviations are requested.
In new buildings (building permit after 02/1989) the obligation to prepare and submit a passive and/or active fire protection study where required is still in force, in accordance with the provisions of article 15 of the PD 71/1988 (GG 32A) as in force.
Category A operators are exempted from the obligation to obtain an (active) fire protection certificate, but must comply with and maintain the fire protection measures and means required by current legislation, which will be reflected in floor plans that are part of the file to be kept in the holding.
Category B - Medium Risk
This includes:
i) public gathering places with a theoretical population (as calculated on the basis of the applicable fire-fighting legislation) of more than 150 persons as well as public gathering places regardless of capacity that use LPG (bottles or tanks) for their operational needs and
ii) stores (food retailers or service stores) of over 1.000 square meters as well as stores, independently of their area, that store LPG cylinders over 200 kg.
In category B, the operators must, within fifty (50) days from the date of submission of the notification, take all the necessary actions in order to be provided by the relevant Fire Service with an (active) fire protection certificate, which will be kept in the business file.
Category C - High Risk
This includes: Theatres and cinemas. 
In category C, the operators must, before the date of submission of the notification, take all the necessary actions in order to have been provided by the relevant Fire Service with a certificate of (active) fire protection which will be kept in the installation file.

Title
Start-up Disclosure titled: Notification of Operation (Article 167 of Law 44422/2016 (A 230) of a Maintenance or Repair Garage for Cars, Motorcycles, Mopeds, Normal and heavy vehicles.
Notes:
The notification of the opening of a maintenance or repair workshop for cars, motorcycles, motorcycles, mopeds is made according to the model of the annex of the No. 314766 (FEK B 5272/12.11.2021) ministerial decision. The same template also applies to the notification of any change in the original for the operation of the workshop, such as change of data, change of operator, change of place of activity, etc.
The notification includes the necessary information on the activity carried out and is submitted by the operator of the activity, who is solely responsible for the information contained therein. No supporting documents shall be submitted with the notification.
The operator of the workshop must keep the required supporting documents, as per Article 4 of the prot. No. 314766/2021 (FEK 5272 B), along with the proof of submission of all notifications of the operation of the establishment, at the place where the activity is carried out.

Description

Notes:
CHANGE OF NOTIFICATION If the details of the notification of establishment and operation of the tourist road transport undertaking need to be changed, the operator of the activity must provide prior notification of the intended change. The procedure to be followed for submitting notifications concerning information to be changed is the same as the procedure for the initial notification described in Article 3 of Joint Ministerial Decision No 18913/2021.
In particular, if the change consists of a change in the operator of the activity pursuant to Article 9 of Law 4442/2016, both the old and the new operator must submit a notification of the change within ten (10) days of the change. The notification only concerns information about the operator of the activity. The road transport operator authorisation will be issued to the new operator.
If the activity comes to an end at the site where it has been taking place, the operator must provide notice of this. The procedure to be followed for submitting notifications of cessation of operations is the same as the procedure for the initial notification described in Article 3 of Joint Ministerial Decision No 18913/2021.
If the location where the activity is carried out changes, the operator must submit a new notification concerning the new location of the activity.

Description
The procedure relates to the granting of an operating licence to private companies (sole proprietorship), which provide third parties with one or more of the following services:
a. surveillance or guarding of movable or immovable property and facilities;
b. protection of natural persons;
c. secure transportation, using specially-modified armoured vehicles, of money, bond certificates, antiquities, works of art and other items of value;
d. security guard protection for shows, exhibitions, conferences, competitions and sporting events;
e. security checks for pilots / cabin crews, passengers, cabin baggage, check-in baggage, cargo and items for posting at airports and ports, as well as access control to premises and installations in general thereof, with the approval of the competent aviation or port authority;
f. escort services for the safe movement of vehicles carrying bulky or heavy objects, using special vehicles bearing the appropriate signage and indications;
g. escort services for sports team delegations to ensure their safe transport;
h. preparation of studies and the design of measures to ensure the safe conduct of the activities in cases a) to g);
i. installation, maintenance and monitoring of the operation of machinery and security systems and alarm systems, other than those installed in vehicles;
k. operation of centres for the reception, control and transmission of alarm signals, and
j. preparation of studies and design of security systems, with regard to the activities in cases i) and j).

Notes
The competent fire service (offices or local fire safety prevention and suppression departments) may issue a one-time temporary (active) fire protection certificate, after the submission of the respective application and supporting documents as indicated in Item 1 of Annex C to Fire Service Regulation No 13/2021 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5519), accompanied by a reasoned report from the operator, to business undertakings and facilities that:
a) fall within the scope of Article 1(2) of Fire Service Regulation No 13/2021 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5519), but have not fully completed their obligation to install a permanent water-based fire suppression network or an automatic fire suppression system.
b) fall within the scope of Article 1(2.1) of Fire Service Regulation No 13/2021 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5519), but for which deviations from the passive fire protection study description have been identified, which affect aspects of the active fire protection study (Annex B).
c) fall within the scope of Article 1(2.2) and (2.3) of Fire Service Regulation No 13/2021 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5519), but which have not fully implemented their obligations with regard to integrated structural fire protection features.
Unless otherwise stipulated by fire department or special fire protection provisions, the duration of the temporary (active) fire protection certificate may not exceed six (6) months.
Undertakings and facilities that have already been granted a temporary (active) fire protection certificate do not have the right to seek reissue.
A prerequisite for the granting of a temporary (active) fire protection certificate is completion of the remaining fire protection measures and the installation of equipment provided for in the respective study. This certificate shall also specify any additional or increased fire protection measures and equipment required by the fire department and the deadlines by which they must be completed.
As of entry into force of Fire Service Regulation No 13/2021 (Government Gazette, Series II, No 5519), paragraph 63 of Joint Ministerial Decision No 3021/19/6/1986 ‘Limitation of certificates and other supporting documents required by the current provisions for the processing of citizens’ cases by public sector services’ is no longer applicable (Government Gazette, Series II, No 847).

Access to the ‘E-Authorities’, with regard to the adoption of the administrative fire protection acts, shall be carried out through the Single Digital Portal of Public Administration (Gov.gr), which shall be used by all stakeholders in the procedures for the adoption of those acts, namely the competent Firefighting Services (Futures or Local DCFS).
Access to ‘e-Licences’ for the issuing of administrative fire protection acts is via the Public Administration’s Single Digital Portal (gov.gr), which is used by all parties involved in procedures for issuing the abovementioned documents, namely the competent fire service (offices or local fire safety prevention and suppression departments) and authorised administrators.
